challenge.method: Opened the exact FAQ at line 106 and identified which question each answer addresses. Compared its versioned-text links, document-reuse answer, treatment of substantive and cosmetic modifications, and translation passages with the English-authority statement on the edition page.
challenge.results: Line 106 answers a CLA question. Lines 108–110 directly authorize unchanged reuse of the license document. Lines 112–118 treat a substantive edit as a different license and distinguish cosmetic changes. Lines 132–138 describe a translation as a convenience and reserve authority to English. Neither a substantive draft nor a translation is the unchanged English document assessed here. [ASF FAQ](https://www.apache.org/foundation/license-faq.html) [ASF edition page](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0)

limitations: The conclusion covers the complete unchanged official English document. Substantive edits, translations, trademark use, and compliance for a software distribution fall outside it.
The FAQ was observed as rendered lines. The plaintext digest identifies the document being copied. The Web response supplied no raw-HTML digest or byte offsets for the FAQ.
reasoning: ASF expressly permits unchanged reuse in its FAQ answer about the Apache License 2.0 document itself. The FAQ identifies the versioned plaintext, and ASF identifies English as authoritative. Together these support copying the complete, unchanged English document identified in the claim.
